entry.name: Inn in the Samaritan parable
entry.note: Unnamed inn inside the narrated story in Luke 10:34–35, where the Samaritan brings the injured traveler and pays the host. Distinct from the road and from the framing conversation. The text gives an inn, not a specific architectural description.

result.appearanceFromText: The text names only an inn where the Samaritan brings the injured traveler and leaves him in the host's care; no architecture is described, so the stone-village inn of Roman Judea is supplied from the era brief.

stages.label: Roadside inn
stages.when: Roman Judea, the road between Jerusalem and Jericho

quotes.quote: brought him to an inn, and took care of him

stages.text: Roadside inn: a modest two-storey inn of pale limestone blocks on the Jerusalem to Jericho road in Roman Judea, with a flat roof, a low arched gateway wide enough for a laden animal, and an open courtyard with a stone well and a water trough. Scrub and dry terraces of olive and fig stand behind it, and the rough track runs past its gate.
